fatal_errors: The proposed acid-dealloying intervention is unrelated to the target closed-loop high-throughput synthesis, post-ageing screening, machine-learning prediction, and Bayesian optimisation campaign.

The hypothesis assumes a homogeneous high-entropy solid-solution starting material, whereas the target fresh catalysts commonly contained agglomerates of fine metallic particles and spanned diverse five- to nineteen-element supported compositions.
The claimed enhancement through M–N bonding has no mechanistic basis in the proposed acid-etching treatment because no nitrogen-introduction step is specified.
None of the cited evidence directly demonstrates acid-dealloyed Pt-rich shells improving supported multimetal catalysts under automotive exhaust, water, NO, or severe 900 °C ageing conditions.
The decisive target mechanism—ageing-induced Cu–Pt electronic reconstruction, detrimental Pt–Ni/Fe coordination, and hydrocarbon-assisted NO reduction—is absent.
The proposed 100–300 °C boundary omits the severe 900 °C cyclic lean/rich ageing that defines the target durability problem.
explanation: The response addresses the broad goal of improving a low-PGM multielement automotive catalyst and offers a testable treated-versus-untreated comparison, so it has limited problem alignment and experimental value. However, it does not reconstruct the target intervention, catalyst state, benchmark, operating protocol, mechanism, or quantitative outcomes. The target used automated exploration of composition and solvothermal processing, with post-ageing performance against Pd and random exploration as the principal baselines. The generated hypothesis instead proposes acid dealloying and a Pt-rich shell without direct evidence in automotive exhaust catalysis. E1 concerns controlled synthesis of noble-metal HEAs, E2 concerns nitrogen-doped Pt-rich HEAs for electrochemical ORR, and E3 concerns high-entropy oxides for OER; these provide only remote analogy and do not validate the proposed treatment or exhaust mechanism. The falsification experiment is directionally reasonable but lacks a defined exhaust composition, severe ageing protocol, species-resolved thresholds, and an appropriate Pd benchmark.
